title: What is known about 1RB0RC_1LC0RD_0LD0LC_1RE0LA_0RA0RF_0LA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RC_1LC0RD_0LD0LC_1RE0LA_0RA0RF_0LA---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The machine is a base-5 counter, incremented once per sweep, whose digits drift and collide; Lean proves the counting rule for all configurations, and an exact simulator of that structure finds no halt in the first 1016 steps. Halting needs a crowded collision that the run has never produced, and nothing proves it never will.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: The piece rules of a visit
claims.text: Nine rules, each for all counts and all surrounding tape: the crossing of the left gap, the carry over a d, the turn at a, b, c or e, the return over a gap and over a passed d, and the growth at the left end.

claims.title: One visit is one base-5 increment
claims.text: From a sample configuration 0 0 W^g X₁ W^g₁ … Xₖ W^gₖ T with digits a, b, c, d, e (values 1, 2, 3, 4, 0), whenever the increment bump is defined (the carry stops at a digit with a nonempty gap after it), the machine reaches the sample configuration of the incremented counter in exactly 10g + 11 + cost steps; iterated in run_sound.

claims.title: The merge of two adjacent e
claims.text: The visit that meets two e side by side, the place where the four machines of the family differ: the pair becomes the word 001, and a new digit a is born at the left end of the tape.

claims.title: From blank tape into the counter
claims.text: After 1,001,215 steps the run is at a sample configuration made of standard digits, and the counter rule alone carries it through the next 198 visits.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>16</sup> steps
claims.text: The visit-level simulator py/vsim.py (runs each visit on a copy with long gaps cut short and puts them back; identical to the direct simulator on all sample configurations of the first 3·107 steps) runs 1016 steps, 75,701,323 visits, without a halt. The near miss D>0 1 0 occurs 8 times in the first 1015 steps.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt.

claims.title: Collisions are where it could halt
claims.text: 99.988% of the visits are plain increments. The others are overflows (all digits d) and collisions of a digit with the next. Hand-made tapes with crowded collisions reach D>0 1 1 and halt; the run has met only isolated collisions so far.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. It would take control of the gaps at every collision of the counter, forever.

check: cd holdouts/1RB0RC_1LC0RD_0LD0LC_1RE0LA_0RA0RF_0LA---/py && python3 vsim.py 1RB0RC_1LC0RD_0LD0LC_1RE0LA_0RA0RF_0LA--- A 1e15 D     # about 3 minutes

explainer.lede: A six-state machine that counts in base 5. Its digits are little defects in a periodic tape; each sweep of the head adds one to the number; the digits drift across the tape, overflow, and now and then crash into each other. Nobody knows whether one of those crashes will stop it. No halt in the first 10<sup>16</sup> steps.

facts.text: One sweep = one increment, proved for all configurations.
No halt in the exact visit simulator.
The only place a halt can come from.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.549). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 80,974 cells (66,101 left of the start, 43 right), with a density of 1s of 0.351.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: What the tape is made of
html: Stop the machine each time its head stands on the leftmost cell of the tape in state A (a sample configuration). The tape then always reads the same way: a long periodic background of the four-cell word W = 0001, interrupted by a few short defects, and closed on the right by a fixed wall 001 that hardly ever moves. The left end grows by three cells per sample.

Almost every defect is one of five words, which we call digits and give values:

digitcellsvalueafter the visitgaps
a00111b = 2one W fewer after it
b00110012c = 3—
c0011013d = 4—
d001114e = 0carry: the head goes on to the next digit
e001010a = 1one W moves from the gap after it to the gap before it

So the tape is 0 0 Wg0 X1 Wg1 X2 … Xk Wgk 0 0 1: a left gap of g0 copies of W, then digits, each followed by its own gap. A sixth defect, the single extra 0 (written z), is an empty digit; it appears when the counter overflows (below).

sections.heading: One visit is one increment
html: Between two sample configurations the head makes one visit: it runs right through the left gap (turning each 0001 into 1010 as it goes, 10 steps per W there and back), reaches the first digit, and acts on it. A d (value 4) becomes e (value 0) and the head runs on to the next digit: a carry. Any other digit takes one step up (a→b→c→d, e→a) and the head turns back, restoring the background on its way to the left end, where it adds three cells. Read with the first digit as the least significant, the digits are a base-5 counter, incremented once per visit.

The increment also moves the digits. a→b and e→a each take one W from the gap after the digit; e→a gives it to the gap before; every visit adds a W to the left gap. In cells, a digit moves 9 cells to the right per 5 increments, while the left end moves 3 cells left per visit. Digit i is incremented once every 5i visits, so the lowest digit runs right at about 1.8 cells per visit, the next at a fifth of that, and the high digits barely move: every digit slowly catches up with the next one.
Step through real stretches of the run (computed by the exact visit simulator; the counter is shown with the most significant digit first):

Exactly: if the digits after the left gap are d…d X with X ≠ d and at least one W after X, the visit takes 10·g0 + 11 + ∑passed d(10·gi + 24) + 24 steps and gives the counter plus one with the gaps moved as above. Lean proves this for every list of digits and gaps and every tape beyond (visit in lean/Counter.lean); in the run it describes 99.988% of all visits.

sections.heading: Digits are born, drift and collide
html: Every twelfth sample configuration of the first 30,000 visits, one row each, time going down; each defect is a dot at its distance from the right end of the tape. The black line is the left end, moving left; a line that starts on it is a digit born there.
Three things happen, and only three:

• Drift. The lowest digit starts at the left end and runs right at about 1.8 cells per visit; higher digits crawl, the highest stand almost still near the wall.
  • Overflow. When every digit is d (the counter reads 44…4), the carry runs into the wall. All the d become empty digits z, the wall moves a few cells to the right, and a new digit is born at the left end. The counter gains a digit.
  • Collision. When the lowest digit reaches the next one (the gap between them runs out), the two stand side by side and the plain rule no longer applies. The gap runs out on an a→b or e→a step, so a collision starts as a or b next to any of the five digits. For a few increments the pair forms compound words; then it fuses into a single digit (the counter loses a digit and its value jumps), or it leaves a phase defect 001, and the next visit gives birth to a new lowest digit at the left end.

Overflows and collisions are rare: in the first 1013 steps they touch 315 of 2,570,989 visits. Between them the machine is a clean base-5 counter whose digits spread across a tape of width about the square root of the step count. That is the fixed/sqrt growth of the triage.

sections.heading: A near miss inside some collisions
html: The machine halts only in state F reading a 1. It gets there only from state D reading 0 1: D writes a 1 and moves right, E reads that 1, erases it and moves right in state F, and F halts on a 1 (in the usual case D>0 0, E reads the 0 and goes on in state A). So it halts exactly when the head, in state D, finds 0 1 1. In the background and in every plain visit, D always finds 0 0.

D>0 1 does happen, but only inside a few kinds of collision (for example when two e meet), and there the next cell has always been a 0. In the first 1015 steps it happened 8 times, each time followed by 0. Configurations built by hand with crowded digits (several collisions at once, or compound words next to each other) do reach 0 1 1 and halt: 633 of 2,000 random tapes with gaps of 0 to 3 halted within 3·106 steps. So the question is whether the counter ever crowds its digits that badly. That depends on the exact gaps at the moment of each collision, which depend on the whole history of the counter.

sections.heading: Where the four machines part ways
html: This machine and three others, 1RB0LD_0LB1RC_0RD---_1RE0RF_1LF0RA_0LA0LF, 1RB0RC_1LC0RD_0LD0LC_1RE0LA_0RA0RF_0LC---, 1RB0RC_1LC0RD_0LD0LC_1RE0LA_0RA0RF_0RA---, run exactly the same counter: the same tape at every sample configuration, up to renaming the states. 1RB0LD_0LB1RC_0RD---_1RE0RF_1LF0RA_0LA0LF steps over each 0 0 in four steps where the other three take two (so 12 steps per W per visit against 10; 10 here), with the same result; the three others differ from each other only in what follows the near miss. So the four runs first part ways at the first 0 1 0 (step 49,361 for the first machine, 49,247 for the others), and again at every later one. The commonest case is two e side by side:

machinetwo e side by side become
1RB0LD_0LB1RC_0RD---_1RE0RF_1LF0RA_0LA0LFthe pair becomes one digit d (value 4), three W further right.
1RB0RC_1LC0RD_0LD0LC_1RE0LA_0RA0RF_0LA--- (this one)the pair becomes the word 001, and a new digit a is born at the left end of the tape.
1RB0RC_1LC0RD_0LD0LC_1RE0LA_0RA0RF_0LC---the pair becomes a single 0 (an empty digit, a phase defect 00001).
1RB0RC_1LC0RD_0LD0LC_1RE0LA_0RA0RF_0RA---the pair becomes one digit e (value 0).
After that the four runs are different counters with the same rules, and they collide differently. Each one is open for the same reason.

sections.heading: What is proved, and what is left
html:
• Lean, kernel: the nine piece rules of a visit for all counts (lean/Pieces.lean); visit: one visit is one base-5 increment with the gap moves above, for every configuration where the increment is defined (lean/Counter.lean); the merge of two adjacent e (lean/Merge.lean).
  • Lean, native_decide: the run from blank tape reaches a sample configuration of standard digits after 1,001,215 steps, and the counter rule alone then carries it 198 more visits (reach, counted in lean/Reach.lean).
  • Computed: an exact visit-level simulator (py/vsim.py, identical to the direct simulator on every sample configuration of the first 3·107 steps) finds no halt in the first 1016 steps (75,701,323 visits).
  • Open: the collisions. A proof of non-halting would need to show that the counter never brings its digits into a crowded collision that reads 0 1 1, which needs control of all the gaps at once.

family: base-5 counter with drifting, colliding digits
summary: A base-5 counter whose digits are defects in a 0001 background; each sweep adds one; the digits drift right and collide, and a near miss of the halt occurs inside some collisions.
